text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: surge of model load failures for model 'rlm-large-epoch2' in eu-central. Failure pattern: deserialization errors then container restarts. Started ~2061122200. Paging oncall.
Jordan (oncall): I'm up. pulling logs and health metrics.
Jordan (oncall): customer-impact: a handful of hosted endpoints returning 502/503, plus one Dedicated tenant seeing steady errors. tagging CS.
cs-tina: got it. customer reported degraded responses and intermittent rejects. requesting ETA and mitigation steps.
Nina (SRE): cluster-side: nodes eu-ssd-03 and eu-ssd-05 showing frequent kubelet restarts and GPU driver reconnects. dmesg shows GPU reset events.
Sam (Runtime): runtime logs from pod serve-eu-07 show repeated failures during model DeserializeWeights:
```
[ERROR] deserialize.cpp: malformed weight section at offset 0x1f03
[WARN] attempted fallback deserialization -> copying to GPU requires 8.2GiB, only 2.1GiB available
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```
Ishaan (ML): malformed weight section suggests we might be hitting corrupted checkpoint or partial artifact from upstream. but we've also seen OOMs in similar windows before when concurrent JITs + warmups happen.
Jordan (oncall): hypothesis: concurrent warmups + active JITs + node flaps -> memory fragmentation -> deserialization fails and process crashes, causing container to restart and triggers more warmups. vicious cycle.
Sam (Runtime): immediate mitigations I can do:
- disable auto-warmup on pool eu-central-gpu
- route traffic to rlm-large-epoch2-quant-min variant
- reduce concurrent load of canary/warmup controllers
Ishaan (ML): quant-min variant has slightly lower quality but acceptable for mitigation.
Jordan (oncall): do it. also increase container restart backoff to avoid thundering restarts while we stabilize.
deploy-bot: applying change: set route(eu-central-gpu)->rlm-large-epoch2-quant-min, disable-warmup=true. change-id deploy-2061122334-A
Sam (Runtime): change applied. bumping kube restartBackoff to 120s for rlm pods.
Nina (SRE): I'm isolating eu-ssd-05 and cordoning eu-ssd-03 to prevent scheduling. draining non-critical workloads off eu-ssd-02 as well to free GPU memory.
ops-lee: standing by to spin up +3 aux GPU nodes in eu-central if required.
Jordan (oncall): observation: after routing to quant-min and disabling warmup, error rates dropped from ~7% to 1.2% in 4 minutes. Dedicated tenant still seeing sporadic 5xxs, might be on pinned nodes.
cs-tina: relaying to customer: "we have routed traffic to a compatible reduced-precision variant and are evacuating unstable nodes. Full restore ETA TBD; will update within 30m." customer asked about data loss — confirm none.
Sam (Runtime): confirming no inference data loss; only failed requests.
Ishaan (ML): for root cause: two nodes had intermittent GPU driver flaps (likely platform upgrade jobs earlier) which coincided with heavy model reloads; deserialization likely retried concurrently on remaining nodes causing spike in memory allocations and some corrupted reads.
Jordan (oncall): next steps for recovery: 1) rotate traffic back to full precision on stable nodes only; 2) prime JIT cache on a canary pod per node (serially) rather than all at once; 3) coordinate with infra to validate GPU drivers on eu-ssd-05.
Nina (SRE): prepping canary sequence: will allow single-node canary with RW_MAX_CONCURRENT_JIT=1 and RW_DESER_CHUNK=512MB to reduce peak.
Sam (Runtime): also increasing compile timeout from 300s -> 600s to reduce timeouts causing aborts while drivers reconnect.
Jordan (oncall): good. please capture metrics: GPU mem usage per pod, nvml reset counts, container restart counts.
Nina (SRE): attaching quick snapshot (abbreviated):
```
node eu-ssd-02: gpu0 used 14955MiB/16384MiB, resets: 0
node eu-ssd-03: gpu0 used 16020MiB/16384MiB, resets: 3
node eu-ssd-05: gpu0 used 15300MiB/16384MiB, resets: 7
```
Jordan (oncall): ops-lee, please hold on scaling until we stabilize; we may need capacity but want to avoid mixing driver versions.
ops-lee: acknowledged, will keep extra nodes in reserve.
Ishaan (ML): small code change pushed to reduce peak deserialization buffer allocation (ml/opt/2061). Can we test in canary? saves ~35% mem during load.
Sam (Runtime): deploying ML patch to 1 canary pod on eu-ssd-02 with serial JIT priming.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: deploy-2061122334-B (1 pod on eu-ssd-02)
Jordan (oncall): monitoring canary.
Nina (SRE): canary load sequence completed: deserialization mem peak reduced, no driver resets observed on that node during priming.
Jordan (oncall): excellent. next: slowly roll full-precision variant back to stable nodes only with staggered warmups (interval 5m between nodes).
Sam (Runtime): initiating staggered rollout: set warmup-stagger=5m and max-warmup-per-node=1.
Jordan (oncall): handing off to Nina for next shift. objectives for Nina: observe 30m of stable metrics, verify dedicated tenant 5xxs resolved, coordinate with infra to remediate driver on eu-ssd-05.
Nina (SRE): ACK. will update thread on any regression. also will file incident follow-up with timeline and suggested platform driver checks.
cs-tina: letting customers know we're beginning staggered restore; will keep them updated on progress and ETA.
Jordan (oncall): incident severity downgraded to P2 at 2061122610. leaving detailed notes in ticket. thanks all.
incident-bot: responders: Jordan, Nina, Sam, Ishaan, ops-lee, cs-tina. :white_check_mark:
